title: Maximum Valid Pairs Within d
statement:
You are given two arrays `arr1` (length `n`) and `arr2` (length `m`) and an integer `d`.

Form pairs `(arr1[i], arr2[j])` that satisfy

`arr1[i] <= arr2[j] <= arr1[i] + d`

Each element of either array can be used in **at most one** pair. Return the **maximum number of pairs** that can be formed.
inputFormat:
The first line contains three integers `n`, `m` and `d`.
The second line contains `n` integers: `arr1`.
The third line contains `m` integers: `arr2`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of pairs.

examples.explanation: Pair (20, 25) because 20 <= 25 <= 30, and pair (45, 50) because 45 <= 50 <= 55. Only two elements of arr2 exist, so 2 is the maximum.
Pair (1, 2) and pair (2, 2). Element 3 would need a partner in [3, 4] and the remaining 9 is too large.
Both 5s could accept 7, but 7 can only be used once.

complexity.time: O(n log n + m log m)

hints: Sorting both arrays lets you compare candidates in order instead of searching all pairs.
Look at the smallest unmatched value of each array. If the arr2 value is below the arr1 value, it can never be used with this or any later arr1 value.
If the arr2 value is above arr1[i] + d, then arr1[i] can never be matched with this or any later arr2 value. Otherwise pair them greedily.
